discovery: Direct observation of Anderson localization of matter waves in disordered potentials using ultracold atoms

nominees.name: Massimo Inguscio
nominees.affiliation: LENS and University of Florence; CNR-INO, Italy

nominees.name: Alain Aspect
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Optique Graduate School, Université Paris-Saclay, CNRS, France

nominees.name: Giovanni Modugno
nominees.affiliation: University of Florence and LENS; CNR-INO, Italy

motivation: Anderson's 1958 prediction that disorder can halt wave transport is one of the deepest ideas in the physics of disordered systems. For fifty years it was hard to test cleanly in matter, because interactions, decoherence and absorption obscure it in solids. In 2008 two groups observed it directly. In Florence, Inguscio and Modugno used a non-interacting Bose-Einstein condensate in a quasi-periodic lattice and saw the Aubry-André localization transition. In Palaiseau, Aspect's group imaged the exponential profiles of atoms localized in laser speckle. These experiments made disorder a controllable parameter. They opened controlled studies of the interplay between disorder and interactions, including many-body localization, the Bose glass and three-dimensional mobility edges. This is a simple question that was very hard to answer, and the answer launched a field that connects condensed matter, statistical physics and quantum simulation.
